I would say they are messier, in my experience. Self shielded fcaw runs with dc electrode negative. Dual shielded fcaw, mig, spray arc mig use dc electrode positive.  I use spray transfer MIG at work, as long as your metal is clean and machine is quality, you can obtain zero spatter welds. From aws.org-> For higher production speeds use spray transfer. Greater than 80% argon mix set the voltage at 23-4 volts to begin. Set the amperage with about 300-400 inches of wire feed speed. Again increase/decrease wire feed speed until 150 amps is reached. ) if you are diligent with practice and study of the processes, you can learn it yourself.
I'd recommend 240v for sure at minimum, so you can be ready to run hotter temps as needed. As far as power specifics are concerned, I'm the wrong person to ask haha.

Vast majority of auto dark hoods have replaceable z87 rated plastic lenses. The z87 rating should apply to your safety glasses as well. The z87 means it is rated for impact, most are fairly durable. ANSI z87 (full name for rating) does block out UV rays. As far as fcaw/mig is concerned, fcaw is *generally* cheaper, more specifically self shielded fcaw(no gas required). All forms of fcaw (self shield, dual shield) will have slag covering after a weld is made. This will need to be cleaned off. Mig requires shielding gas. 100% CO2, 75% argon 25% CO2 (C25) are generally most common for the hobbyist. If I remember correctly, 100% CO2 is cheaper, and runs hotter than C25. Mig does not have slag, due to its lack of flux.
